findings.claim: Composition total duration is 90s across 9 scenes
findings.actual: index.html root element has data-duration="30", not 90. GSAP timeline only covers 0–30s with 7 scenes (S1–S7 in HTML). Spec describes 9 scenes totaling 90s (S0–S8) including MLAuto BG, Robot emergence, Particle Morph, Climax Stats Slam, and CTA Finale — none of those are implemented.
findings.remediation: Change root data-duration from 30 to 90. Add missing scenes: S0 (cold open), S2 v3 (particle morph), S5 v3 (Robot 2), S6 v3 (marketplace+schedule), S7 v3 (stats slam), S8 (CTA finale). Note: scene IDs in index.html (s1–s7) do NOT map 1:1 to spec scene IDs (S0–S8) — index.html is an earlier 30s draft, not a 90s composition.

findings.claim: ease: 'out-quint' used for phone entry (y:400→0, scale:0.85→1, duration:0.7)
findings.actual: 'out-quint' is NOT a valid GSAP 3 ease string. GSAP 3 uses 'power3.out' (equivalent) or 'quint.out' (legacy alias, not guaranteed in 3.14.2 without EasePack). The correct GSAP 3 string is 'power3.out'. index.html correctly uses 'back.out(1.2)' for phone entry animations, not 'out-quint'.
findings.remediation: Replace 'out-quint' with 'power3.out' in implementation. The spec table entry should read: ease:'power3.out'. This is a spec authoring error.

findings.actual: The mulberry32 code in the spec is correct and matches the canonical implementation. The hash step using Math.imul with the two mixing passes (t^t>>>15 * t|1, then t^t + Math.imul(t^t>>>7, t|61)) is accurate. The final (t^t>>>14)>>>0 / 4294967296 produces a float in [0,1). This is the correct mulberry32 algorithm. Math.imul is available in all modern browsers. No issues.

findings.claim: All clips have data-start, data-duration, data-track-index attributes. No Math.random() in composition.
findings.actual: Existing clips in index.html (#s1–#s7) correctly use data-start, data-duration, data-track-index on every .clip div. No Math.random() is present in the current JS. The root #root element has data-composition-id='main', data-start=0, data-duration=30, data-width=1080, data-height=1920 — all correct HyperFrames attributes. HOWEVER: window.__timelines['main'] = tl at the end is the correct HyperFrames timeline registration pattern. The 90s scenes not yet implemented cannot be verified for constraint compliance.
findings.remediation: When adding new scene clips, ensure every element using .clip class has all three required data-* attributes. The seeded mulberry32 must replace any Math.random() call — spec correctly mandates this.

findings.actual: Spec scene durations sum correctly: 4+8+10+10+16+10+12+10+10 = 90s. Timing is internally consistent. HOWEVER: index.html implements a 30s composition with 7 scenes with different scene content and different timing. The 30s draft is NOT the same as the 90s spec — it is an earlier proof-of-concept. All 9 spec scenes need to be built from scratch or the 30s draft extended.
findings.remediation: The 90s timing math is correct and usable. Update data-duration on #root to 90. Scenes S4–S8 need to be added as new clip divs. Scenes S0–S3 need to replace/augment the current 0–30s clips.

findings.claim: OPR timecode sync points (bass drops) for flash event alignment
findings.actual: Open Question #1 is unresolved. No timecodes specified for flash events. S0 flash at 3.8s, S1 flash at 5.0s, S7 impacts at 70.0/72.5/75.0s, S8 final flash at 87.0s — all these require manual audio analysis to align with actual bass hits in the OPR track. Without this, flash events will be misaligned.
findings.remediation: Load the MP3 in an audio editor (Audacity, Adobe Audition) or use ffprobe with beat detection. Map bass onset times. Then hard-code those exact seconds as GSAP keyframe positions. This BLOCKS correct implementation of all flash/slam timing.
